It is nacre, the shimmering inner layer of mollusk shells.

post.caption: Mother of pearl's rainbow isn't pigment. It is nacre, the shimmering inner layer of mollusk shells. It is also the material that coats a pearl. Nacre is mostly aragonite, a mineral with chalk's chemical recipe. That mineral forms microscopic plates, stacked in overlapping layers. Each plate is only about half a micrometer thick. Light bouncing off and between those layers makes the rainbow shimmer. Tilt a piece, and the colors shift. Gem labs call the shimmer on a pearl orient. Aragonite is brittle, yet nacre is far tougher than the mineral alone. One studied pearl had 2,615 layers, built over 548 days.
